About Agoda
At Agoda, we bridge the world through travel. Our story began in 2005, when two lifelong friends and entrepreneurs, driven by their passion for travel, launched Agoda to make it easier for everyone to explore the world.
Today, we are part of Booking Holdings [NASDAQ: BKNG], with a diverse team of over 7,000 people from 90 countries, working together in offices around the globe. Every day, we connect people to destinations and experiences, with our great deals across our millions of hotels and holiday properties, flights, and experiences worldwide.
No two days are the same at Agoda. Data and technology are at the heart of our culture, fueling our curiosity and innovation. If you’re ready to begin your best journey and help build travel for the world, join us.

s.h: Get to Know Our Design Team
s.t:
The Design team is a diverse group of product designers and researchers that help to build Agoda’s products from our home office in Bangkok. Being a product-driven company, we constantly partner with product managers and engineers to understand user problems and design workflows, interactions, and visual interfaces.
There is always an opportunity for growth here. Focus on your craft to improve or expand your skill set, or step into a managerial role and flex your talents as a designer and driver of team projects. This is a great time to join a team that’s small enough to be scrappy and hands on, yet big enough to influence change and product strategy.
At Agoda, we offer a range of travel products – including accommodations, flights, and activities – and are building the next generation of travel experiences to help customers plan and book their entire trip. Join our design team to shape how users engage with recommendations, making them personalized, contextual, and relevant.
As a Product Designer L2 / Senior Product Designer, Trip Marketing , you’ll lead the design of cross-sell and recommendation across all of our user touchpoints. You’ll partner closely with engineers, user researchers, and product managers to design interactions that feel human, helpful, and seamless.
This is a hands-on role where you’ll set UX strategy, drive complex design initiatives, and ensure our experiences are intuitive, scalable, and grounded in user needs.

6+ years of full-time experience as a product designer for digital or web-based products; in-house experience highly preferred.
Create visually stunning, intuitive, and delightful interfaces, and independently deliver pixel-perfect UI and seamless interactions. You sweat the details and care deeply about craft.
You are highly experienced in UI design, with deep knowledge of design patterns and a creative approach to solving problems through user interfaces.
Proficient in both quantitative and qualitative research, with hands-on experience running user interviews, synthesizing findings, and generating actionable insights to inform design decisions.
Take full ownership of the design process for a dedicated scrum, from discovery to delivery. You’ll set the design vision, define the user experience, and ensure high-quality execution.
Partner with Product managers to shape product vision and roadmap. You’ll use data, research, and business context to inform your design decisions, always balancing user needs with business goals.
Has experience of managing multiple stakeholders within an agile development process
Strong communicator who can articulate design rationale, influence stakeholders, and build trust across disciplines.
A strong portfolio of work that demonstrates your design thinking, process, and solutions showcasing beautiful, user-centered web and mobile product design.

Present your work to peers and leadership, async and in-person

s.h: Think and write about your process and detailing your decisions

Champion cohesion and consistency in UX design that unites a growing family of products/features
Be a strategic leader with a vision in how to implement experiences that represent the most customer-centric intersection between design, business, content, and technology.

You work alongside your design partners in driving discovery and ideation workshops and align the group around a vision and approach
You have a track record of crafting sophisticated flows and customer journeys
You can think and craft at a system level, not just interface elements or pages
You’ll regularly make use of your soft skills: listening, negotiating, decision-making
You can balance multiple priorities and successfully deliver in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

Effective articulation of ideas and design solutions
Expressing feedback with kindness and candor
Tolerance for ambiguity and healthy curiosity
Translation of quantitative & qualitative insights into design decisions
Contribution to our culture: motivation, optimism, quality, integrity

About Gusto
At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.
All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy .
AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

The HR Expertise pod builds Gusto's knowledge and guidance layer — the part of the product that makes a small business feel like it has an expert HR team in its corner, not just a software tool. That layer is increasingly AI-driven: AI-generated guidance, AI-drafted documents, AI workflows for human HR advisors, and the compliance knowledge graph underneath all of it.
This role sits at the intersection of service design and AI product design. You'll shape how Gusto delivers HR expertise across two sides of a service: the small business owner asking for help, and the HR expert delivering it. You'll design AI-assisted experiences in a domain where mistakes have legal consequences for our customers — which is exactly why judgment, preference, and craft matter here in a way they don't in lower-stakes products.

The HR Experiences team at Gusto wants to make HR a reliable support for small businesses. They create smart guidance, tools for advisors, and a compliance layer. This helps provide top-quality HR support in a way that feels simple and easy to access.
Gusto Design is operating in an AI-native way, and HRX is one of the teams encouraging that envelope hardest. We expect this role to bring fluency with AI in two directions:
AI in your workflow. Using AI to accelerate exploration, prototyping, research synthesis, and content drafting — so the team moves faster without losing craft.
AI in the product. You will design the user experience for AI-generated outputs. This means showing uncertainty clearly and displaying errors in a user-friendly way. You will also ensure that users can keep control when AI suggestions differ from HR best practices. Additionally, you will create moments for customers or advisors to correct the system if necessary.

Shape the end-to-end experience of HR Assist, HR Partner Console, Compliance Intelligence, and HR Documents — four AI-powered product surfaces that share a common knowledge layer.
Lead service design across the two-sided product: journey maps, service blueprints, and operational handoffs between AI systems, human advisors, and small business customers.
Make judgment calls about AI outputs — when to ship them, when to override them, when to put a human in the loop, and how to articulate why a generated direction is or isn't good enough.
Define how trust, uncertainty, graceful failure, and human override show up across these surfaces — patterns that will inform AI experience design across the broader HRX org.
Co-lead product direction with PM, engineering, and data partners across four teams. You'll be a co-owner of strategy, not a downstream executor of it.
Frame ambiguous problems and align partners around a clear direction, often before the data is in.
Conduct and direct research with customers and HR partners to validate these experiences in a high-stakes compliance domain.

You've shipped AI-powered experiences to production — not prototypes — and can speak concretely to how you handled uncertainty, errors, and human override.
Experience in service design for products that involve two sides or multiple stakeholders. You should have real experience with journey mapping and service blueprinting, including operational handoffs, not just in workshop exercises.
You can evaluate and direct AI-generated design and content — knowing when to use it, when to override it, and how to raise the bar. In a compliance domain, "wrong" isn't just bad UX; it's legal exposure for our customers.
Cross-functional judgment to co-lead direction with PM, engineering, and data — and hold your position when the right answer is unpopular.
Comfort with ambiguity — you frame the problem, scope the work, and advance forward without waiting for perfect information.
5+ years of product design experience owning shipped work in B2B SaaS, with well-developed craft across web. (Figma and a modern design toolchain assumed.)

Experience in a consequential domain — HR, compliance, fintech, legal, or healthcare — where the cost of being wrong is real.
Helped lead a team's shift to AI-native workflows, and can speak to what changed about the work itself, not just the tools.
Background contributing to AI governance, evaluation practices, or AI experience design patterns.
Experience designing for internal operators or expert users (advisors, agents, support staff) alongside customer-facing surfaces.

About Toast
Our focus is on building the platform that helps restaurants adapt, take control, and get back to what they do best: building the businesses they love.

And because our technology is purpose-built for restaurants, by restaurant people, restaurants can trust that we'll deliver on their needs for today while investing in experiences that will power their restaurant of the future. We build experiences that help make operating and growing a business and delighting customers easier and scalable.

It's why tens of thousands of businesses love Toast.
Toast IQ is our AI assistant, designed to give restaurant operators smarter insights, deeper personalization, and the ability to take action across the Toast ecosystem. Building on this foundation, we're investing heavily in agentic capabilities by giving operators the ability to delegate real work to Toast IQ , not just view insights.
We're entering an exciting phase of expanding this product to tens of thousands of businesses. That expansion depends on getting the core interaction patterns right once, and getting the whole company aligned behind them. That's where you come in.

As the Principal Product Designer for Toast IQ Core, you will define the interaction language for agentic experiences at Toast including the patterns, behaviors, and components that every team building on top of Toast IQ will use. This isn't a single-surface design role.

Your job is to figure out what "good" looks like when a restaurant operator moves from viewing a dashboard to delegating work to an AI agent, and then to get product, engineering, and design teams across the company to build on that foundation instead of inventing their own.
You'll set direction hands-on, in Figma, in prototypes, in critique, and through influence: building the conviction and relationships needed for other teams to adopt a pattern language you define, not just execute your own roadmap. You'll partner closely with product, engineering, data science, go-to-market, and conversational and service designers to define the future of intelligence at Toast.
This is a highly visible, individual-contributor role for someone who wants outsized leverage over how an entire product area feels and works.

Systems ownership: Define and evangelize the core interaction patterns, behaviors, and component language for agentic experiences across Toast IQ. Building a system that other designers and teams design on top of, not just shipping your own features.
Organizational influence: Build conviction across product, engineering, and GTM leadership for a UX point of view they didn't already have. Agentic UX at Toast's scale is largely undefined territory, you're not executing an established pattern, you're setting one and getting others to follow it.
Leadership: Proven track record leading high-impact design initiatives at a principal level: defining new interaction paradigms (not just refining existing ones) and driving their adoption beyond your own immediate team.
Execution: Lead end-to-end design for core UX/UI within Toast's AI ecosystem across web and native mobile, driving prototyping and experimentation for AI features like memory, personalization, agentic workflows, and actions.
AI-native design experience: Have shipped a 0-to-1 AI or agentic product experience, not just designed features that use AI under the hood. Deep understanding of emerging AI use cases and tooling, plus foundational user-centered design, usability, and accessibility standards.
Pro-research: Proven ability and desire to conduct and coordinate data analysis, user research, and usability testing to inform design decisions.
Tools: Proficiency with emerging AI tools (Claude, Replit, V0, etc.) is essential, as well as design tools like Figma, Miro, and other collaborative platforms.
Partner collaboration: Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively across product, engineering, GTM, and data science to define requirements and align on goals.
Mentorship: Mentor designers at all levels and act as a design-quality bar-raiser across the org, fostering a culture of innovation and AI adoption.
What we'll ask to see
Case studies that show you defining a new interaction paradigm , not just refining an existing one, and driving adoption of it beyond your own team or product surface. We're evaluating systems thinking and organizational influence as much as visual craft.

You are a dynamic leader with proven impact in previous roles who is ready and willing to take on new challenges! You’re excited to join the remotely distributed group of product designers, user researchers, design ops leaders, and product managers that compose the Toast Design team. You embody the tenets that drive Toast’s Design practice:
You have a founder’s mentality: and exhibit ownership of outcomes over outputs. You own the quality and outcomes associated with full end to end experiences.
You lift others up: and recognize you don’t have to be a manager to engage and exhibit true leadership. You find formal ways to utilize your personal skill set to uplevel those around you.
You drive action through influence: and appreciate that building trusting and productive relationships with those around you is integral to driving action. You build strong relationships to enact influence throughout the entirety of the area of the business you work within.
You build strong perspectives: and guide yourself and your teams to make good decisions quickly and often. You collaboratively make well informed decisions with large scale impact across the area of the business you work within.
You raise the bar: and commit to continually improving the technical skills relevant to your role. You find large scale, creative methods to continually build your skill set.

Vercel is the agentic infrastructure company. We free people and agents to ship what’s next.
For more than a decade, Vercel has shaped how the web is built. As the team behind Next.js, v0, and AI SDK, we create products that help builders move from idea to production with speed, security, and exceptional developer experience.
Now, software is entering a new era, and the next generation of products will not just be used by people. They will be built, extended, and operated by agents.
We are building the platform for that future, trusted by companies like OpenAI, PayPal, Ramp, Supreme, and millions of developers worldwide . Whether you’re building our products, supporting our customers, growing our community, or shaping our story, you’ll help define what comes next.

You’ll help define Growth Design at Vercel and shape the complete self-serve journey: signup, onboarding, first project and deployment, adoption, conversion, expansion, and retention. The work spans people, agents, and the handoffs between them.
You’ll report into Product Design and work closely with Growth Product, Engineering and Data. You’ll have the authority and support to move from an observed problem to a working prototype, shipped experience, and measured result.
Vercel gives you unlimited access to leading LLMs and in-house tools that make product data easier to explore. If a tool limits the work, you can partner directly with its builders or improve it yourself.
This role does not come with a mature Growth Design playbook, stable briefs, or one bounded product surface. Priorities change as evidence arrives. Some experiments will not ship. Our data and tools allow us to validate hypotheses. You should enjoy finding the right problem, making something real, working through implementation, and staying accountable after launch.
If you’re based within a pre-determined commuting distance of one of our offices (SF, NY, London, or Berlin), the role includes in-office anchor days on Monday, Tuesday, and Friday. If you're located beyond that distance, the role is fully remote. For location-specific details, please connect with our recruiting team.

Own the self-serve experience across onboarding, activation, adoption, monetization, and retention for people and agents.
Find high-impact opportunities through customer research, product data, and direct use of Vercel.
Co-own Growth strategy, priorities, hypotheses, and success measures with Growth Product, Engineering, and Data.
Build and test working prototypes using the right tools for the question, including Figma, v0, Cursor, and Claude Code.
Design and ship experiments, stay involved through implementation, and interpret results without losing sight of trust, accessibility, or the broader funnel.
Turn what works into durable product improvements, reusable patterns, and better internal tools. Share the learning so Design and Growth improve with every experiment.

Your portfolio demonstrates strong product design fundamentals and measurable outcomes. It shows how you identified opportunities, understood a funnel, chose what to measure, tested ideas, and improved a shipped product.
You have owned ambiguous, complex work from problem framing through launch and iteration. You create clarity and make progress without waiting for a complete brief.
You can form useful hypotheses, choose success and guardrail measures, and interpret quantitative and qualitative evidence with Data partners.
You build interactive prototypes independently using modern AI tools. You are comfortable prompting, working near code, and learning whatever helps you validate an idea.
You design clear, trustworthy experiences across skill levels and abilities. You care about interaction details, edge cases, language, accessibility, and recovery.
You work directly with Product, Engineering, and Data, explain tradeoffs clearly, seek feedback early, and stay involved through implementation. You know when to use or evolve a system and when a one-off is the fastest responsible way to learn.

Have shipped AI or agent experiences.
Have an engineering background or experience contributing production web code.

Company Overview: Blink Health is the fastest growing healthcare technology company that builds products to make prescriptions accessible and affordable to everybody.

Our two primary products – BlinkRx and Quick Save – remove traditional roadblocks within the current prescription supply chain, resulting in better access to critical medications and improved health outcomes for patients.

BlinkRx is the world’s first pharma-to-patient cloud that offers a digital concierge service for patients who are prescribed branded medications. Patients benefit from transparent low prices, free home delivery, and world-class support on this first-of-its-kind centralized platform.

With BlinkRx, never again will a patient show up at the pharmacy only to discover that they can’t afford their medication, their doctor needs to fill out a form for them, or the pharmacy doesn’t have the medication in stock.

We are a highly collaborative team of builders and operators who invent new ways of working in an industry that historically has resisted innovation. Join us! As Lead Product Designer at BlinkRx, you will support the day-to-day design needs of a cross-functional product team and drive alignment across multiple product areas.

You’ll partner closely with stakeholders, product managers, engineers, and other product designers to help define and execute on BlinkRx’s overall product vision and strategy. You’ll be a vocal advocate for all segments of users and customers and consistently deliver intuitive, well-crafted user experiences for BlinkRx products. Responsibilities:
Craft a modern, engaging user experience that solves both user and business needs.
Organize and facilitate collaborative work sessions and design thinking exercises that span multiple teams or departments.
Utilize user research insights and data analysis to inform design decisions, as well as identify where additional data and research are needed.
Propose and concept new product opportunities that are additive to product strategy and provide value to all patient and user segments.
Define interaction patterns, user flows, and complex information architecture models that support the end-to-end user journey through our products.
Generate low, medium, and high-fidelity wireframes, mockups, and prototypes for products and user interfaces.
Conduct a basic level of generative and evaluative user research including moderation of user sessions, synthesizing feedback, and sharing insights for broader team consumption and action.
Document all product design work, including detailed UI specifications, UX decision making and supporting rationale, and user interview insights.
Identify and develop toolkits and processes that empower team members and scale the design team.

7+ years of product design experience in a similar role or product organization
BA/BS degree in Design, HCI, or equivalent practical experience
Problem-solving skills in complex software applications and platforms.
Excellent storytelling and communication skills, both written and verbal
Demonstrated proficiency in Figma and the Adobe Creative Cloud Suite
A blended skill set of visual design, information architecture, interaction design, various prototyping methods, and basic user research skills
Proven track record of collaborating successfully with a cross-functional product and engineering teams to launch products
Experience leading a style guide or design system initiative and driving organization-wide usage and adoption
Ability to exhibit strong judgement and decision making skills
A comprehensive portfolio of product design case studies that showcase early concepts and iterations, supporting user research, performance metrics, and design processes used throughout the duration of each project.
Why Join Us:It is rare to have a company that both deeply impacts its customers and is able to provide its services across a massive population. At Blink, we have a huge impact on people when they are most vulnerable: at the intersection of their healthcare and finances.

We are also the fastest growing healthcare company in the country and are driving that impact across millions of new patients every year. Our business model not only helps people, but drives economics that allow us to build a generational company.

We are a relentlessly learning, constantly curious, and aggressively collaborative cross-functional team dedicated to inventing new ways to improve the lives of our customers. We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity of all kinds.

Warum diese Rolle, warum jetzt
Wir suchen keine Person, die schöne Mockups baut und dann abwartet.
Wir suchen jemanden, der eine Mobile App anfasst und sie danach besser aussehen lässt. Klarer, konsistenter, plattform gerechter. Jemanden, der iOS von Android unterscheidet, jemanden, dessen Figma-Dateien Entwickler:innen freuen.
Das Feedback aus unserer bisherigen Pipeline war eindeutig: Zu viele Kandidat:innen zeigten starke UX-Thinking-Skills, aber schwache UI-Execution. Deshalb haben wir den Titel bewusst geändert. Diese Rolle ist eine UI-Rolle. Wenn dein Portfolio zeigt, wie du Interfaces baust – nicht nur konzipierst – dann lies weiter.
Über DrAnsay
DrAnsay macht Gesundheitsversorgung zugänglicher. Wir haben 2018 mit dem ersten digitalen Gesundheitsservice angefangen und investieren in z.B. medizinisches Cannabis, Abnehmspritze und Men's Health.
Was uns antreibt: Ownership Over Excuses, wir nehmen Verantwortung, bauen Lösungen und bringen Dinge voran, anstatt zu warten. Clarity Creates Speed, wir kommunizieren klar, dokumentieren Entscheidungen und schaffen Transparenz. Build What Matters, wir fokussieren uns auf echten Impact, nicht auf Perfektion.
Kleines Team, kurze Wege, echte Eigenverantwortung. Kein Investment-Board. Kein Design-by-Committee.
Die Rolle
Du arbeitest direkt im Product-/Design-Team und verantwortest die UI-Execution unserer Mobile App. Keine Endlos-Workshops. Keine Konzept-Spiralen. Du bringst visuelle Qualität auf den Screen, plattformgerecht, entwicklerfreundlich, konsistent.
Contract. 3 Monate, mit realistischer Verlängerungsoption. Remote-first, async-freundlich, klare Absprachen statt Micro-Management.
Das übernimmst du
UI-Design für iOS und Android : Plattformspezifisch, nicht generisch: Human Interface Guidelines und Material Design 3 sind deine Leitplanken
Figma-Arbeit auf Senior-Niveau : Auto Layout, Variablen, Design Tokens, interaktive Komponenten, Dev Mode/Handoff; deine Dateien sind so gebaut, dass Entwickler:innen keine Rückfragen brauchen
Component Library & Design System : Du baust Komponenten, die skalieren: States, Varianten, Tokens, sauber dokumentiert
Visuelle Qualität durchsetzen : Visual Hierarchy, Typografie, Spacing, Farbsystem; du siehst, was nicht stimmt, und du weißt, warum
Pixel-Perfect Delivery : Spezifikationen, Annotations, handoff-ready
UI Motion Basics : Transitions und Micro-Interactions; Grundverständnis da, kein Spezialist nötig
Enge Zusammenarbeit mit Product & Engineering : Async-first, dokumentierte Entscheidungen, saubere Iteration
Das bringst du mit

Portfolio mit mind. 2 gelaunchten nativen Apps (iOS oder Android) mit beschriebener eigener UI-Rolle
Figma-Mastery: Auto Layout, Variablen/Design Tokens, Component Libraries, Prototyping, Dev Mode
Mobile-Plattform-Verständnis: iOS HIG und Android Material Design 3; du weißt, was plattformnative Patterns sind
Visuelle Handwerkskompetenz: Visual Hierarchy, Typografie, Spacing/Grid, Farbsystem, Kontrast
Sauberer Dev-Handoff
Eigenverantwortliches Arbeiten im Remote-Setup, async-first, strukturierte Kommunikation

Design-System-Governance (Versionierung, Contribution Guidelines)
Accessibility auf Mobile (WCAG, iOS/Android Standards)
ProtoPie oder Principle für erweiterte Prototypen
Branchenhintergrund: HealthTech, D2C, FinTech
Deutschkenntnisse (kein Muss, Englisch ist Arbeitssprache)
Das bieten wir
Remote-first : Kein Büro, keine Pflicht-Präsenz
Direkter Impact : Echte App, echte Nutzer:innen, kein internes Tool-Design
Kurze Entscheidungswege : Feedback kommt direkt, konkret, ohne Politikebene
Marktübliche Vergütung : Tagessatz nach Erfahrung und Portfolio; wir kommunizieren das direkt im ersten Gespräch
Faire Zusammenarbeit : Nachhaltiges Leistungsvermögen statt Burnout-Kultur; wir messen Ergebnisse, nicht Online-Zeiten
Verlängerungsoption : Wenn es passt, reden wir nach Monat 2 offen darüber
Hinweis: Das ist ein Freelance-/Contractor-Engagement. Betriebliche Benefits sind nicht Bestandteil dieses Modells. Wir sagen das lieber direkt.
So bewirbst du dich
Kein Motivationsschreiben. Kein 8-seitiger Lebenslauf.

Let’s Tango ! Where Innovation Meets Impact.
At Tango Analytics, we’re all about helping businesses make smarter decisions through powerful technology, insightful data, and a whole lot of collaboration. Whether you're a creative thinker, a strategic planner, a tech wizard, or a customer champion, there's a place for you on our team. We believe work should be meaningful and fun — so if you're ready to make a difference while enjoying the journey, come join us and let's Tango !
We are looking for a Product Designer to join our dynamic and growing Product Design team.

Own end-to-end design for a product area — problem framing through wireframes, prototypes, detailed specs, delivery QA, and iteration for enterprise workflows used by lease administrators, portfolio managers, and facilities teams.
Run discovery with enterprise customers — interviews, usability tests, and workflow observation — and translate findings into design decisions that shape what gets built, not just how it looks.
Build design system foundations — identify reusable patterns, document components, and contribute to the Tango Design System alongside the Director of Product Design and other designers.
Modernize legacy enterprise UX — redesign workflows that work but frustrate, within real constraints: data models that can't change overnight, user habits with embedded muscle memory, and migration paths that don't break production.
Build and validate prototypes. Use AI-powered design and prototyping tools to create coded prototypes for user testing and ship design artifacts directly into the development pipeline.
Partner daily with Product Management, Engineering, QA, and Customer Success. Communicate design rationale to non-designers. Advocate for the user when it's uncomfortable.
Use AI-powered design tools as standard practice for research synthesis, design iteration, prototyping, and cross-team documentation.

4+ years in product design with demonstrated work on complex B2B or enterprise products — multi-step, data-dense workflows with multiple user types and real operational consequences.
A portfolio that shows process, not just polish — research, problem framing, iteration, trade-offs, and outcomes. We need to see how you think.
Comfort with ambiguity and legacy systems — can define the problem when there's no brief, design within constraints you didn't choose, and make progress without waiting for perfect information.
Strong cross-functional partnership — explains design decisions to engineers and PMs without jargon, holds a position with evidence, and changes direction when the evidence points somewhere else.
Deep experience with enterprise workflow design — lease administration, facilities management, project management, or adjacent enterprise SaaS domains preferred. Consumer app portfolios won't translate.
Design system instinct — has identified patterns, documented components, or contributed to a design system. Understands why consistency matters across a product and has opinions about how to get there.
Proficiency in Figma and comfort working with AI-powered design tools for prototyping, research synthesis, and documentation.
Familiarity with modern design practices: continuous discovery, usability testing, and data-driven iteration.

Experience with internationalized products supporting multiple languages and regional markets is a plus. Tango 's platform supports 26 languages across 140+ countries.
Bachelor's degree in design, HCI, or a related field — or equivalent professional experience.

A World-Changing Company

Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

The Palantir Design Team is responsible for the human experience of using our software. Our team is growing rapidly, but we're committed to creating a tight-knit team environment that fosters trust, integrity, empathy, and growth. We work together in realizing a shared product vision, and regularly give feedback and critique to each other.

Designing at Palantir is a varied experience. On a given day, you might be: leading a design sprint for your product team; designing a micro-interaction to make a complex analytical task feel simple; and/or advocating for UX consistency by creating flexible, reusable UI components.

As a Product Design intern, your responsibilities look similar to a full-time designer, with the resources, stability, and mentorship of an established tech company. You’ll work on product teams with minimal supervision and own end-to-end execution of real product features. You will work with fellow Designers, Product Managers, Developers, and Forward Deployed Engineers to refine and evolve the quality of Palantir products.
Interaction and visual design . You'll be involved at every stage of design work. You'll help define early product concepts, flesh out the high-level workflow and micro-interactions of a feature, and execute on a crisp and effective visual design. You should have experience designing and prototyping using tools such as Figma.
User research . We frequently do informal user research, and value people who can be flexible with research processes and methodologies to achieve the right outcome. You'll often visit customer offices to interview and learn from the users we serve. You'll pair qualitative methods (e.g. scripted usability tests and contextual inquiry) with quantitative information, like product and usage metrics.
Deliver and communicate designs in close collaboration . We work closely with product and forward deployed engineers to realize our design ideas. You'll treat engineers and product managers as partners and collaborate with them to prototype and build out products.
Awareness of how software interfaces are built. Familiarity with HTML, CSS, Javascript, and Typescript is appreciated. You don't need to be an expert—just fluent enough to collaborate with engineers, and know what's possible with frontend technologies.
What We Value
Excellent collaboration and communication skills with the ability to build great relationships with engineers, PMs, and other stakeholders, and convey and debate design rationale.
High empathy and dedication to the user, striving to understand and empower them.
An iterative design process. You validate your ideas early (with stakeholders and users) and are thoughtful and intentional in seeking and responding to feedback. You move fast, listen, and adapt. You rapidly incorporate feedback, and prioritize collaboration. You are adept at giving and receiving critiques.
Excitement for solving hard, complex problems. You are excited to design for technically complex and data dense interfaces. You thrive in an environment where you can jump into deep subject matter expertise to define simple, approachable, yet still powerful product experiences.
Willingness to learn and make decisions independently, and the ability to ask questions when needed.
What We Require
Must be planning on graduating in 2028. This should be your final internship before graduating.
A portfolio demonstrating at least one software interface design project. If parts of your portfolio are password-protected, please include your portfolio password under 'Additional Questions' when applying.

happyhotel baut den AI Revenue Manager: eine neue Produktkategorie, die Dashboard-lastige SaaS ablöst und sich für Hoteliers anfühlt wie ein eigener Revenue-Experte auf Abruf – erreichbar über WhatsApp, Telegram und ein fokussiertes Web-UI.

Kein "AI-Feature auf ein bestehendes Produkt geklebt", sondern ein Produkt, das von Grund auf um einen konversationellen Agenten herum gedacht ist. Für diese Mission suchen wir dich als Founding Designer – direkt an der Seite von Marius (Co-founder & CTPO) und Sebastian (Co-founder).
📎 Deine Rolle
Du bist die erste Designerin bzw. der erste Designer in einem frisch formierten Produkt-Team und definierst, wie sich ein AI-Agent im Hotelalltag anfühlen muss, damit ihm ein General Manager sein Pricing anvertraut.

Du beantwortest Fragen, für die es heute schlicht keine Design-Patterns gibt: Wie übergibt ein AI-Agent sauber an einen menschlichen Experten, wenn er unsicher ist? Wie werden AI-Entscheidungen transparent und nachvollziehbar, ohne den Nutzer mit Daten zu erschlagen? Wo hört das Chat-UI auf, wo fängt das Web-UI an?
Du arbeitest noch bevor die erste Zeile Produktivcode geschrieben ist – in Prototypen, mit echten Hoteliers als Beta-Design-Partnern, in täglichem Austausch mit den Foundern.
‍
🤝 Deine Aufgaben
Du definierst das Interaktionsparadigma des Produkts: Wie fühlt sich ein AI Revenue Manager an? Was passiert im Chat, was im Web-UI, was proaktiv, was reaktiv?
Du gestaltest die AI-zu-Mensch-Eskalation – eine der zentralen Produktflächen in unserem hybriden Modell, in dem interne RM-Experten einspringen, wenn die AI nicht sicher genug ist.
Du machst AI-Entscheidungen sichtbar und vertrauenswürdig: jede Empfehlung mit Begründung, jedes Ergebnis nachvollziehbar – das Langzeitgedächtnis des Agenten als erstklassiges Designobjekt.
Du baust schnell testbare Prototypen mit AI-assistierten Tools (Figma Make, v0, Lovable, Cursor, Claude Code) und etablierst sie so, dass auch PM und Engineering eigenständig konsistente Prototypen bauen können – du bist Enabler, nicht Bottleneck.
Du führst gemeinsam mit dem PM einen kontinuierlichen Research-Loop mit ~10 Beta-Design-Partnern und unserem internen RM-Team.
Du entwickelst die visuelle Sprache des neuen Produkts – modern, zugänglich, vertrauenswürdig – konsistent über Chat, Web und Benachrichtigungen. So nah am Code wie möglich.
‍ 💙 Dein Profil
3+ Jahre Product Design in digitalen Produkten, idealerweise SaaS.
Erfahrung im 0-to-1- oder Founding-Kontext – du kannst unter Ambiguität entscheiden und brauchst keinen Detail-Brief.
Echtes Interesse an AI-Produkten – nicht "AI-Buzzword im Lebenslauf", sondern Lust, die UX-Patterns für agentic products mitzuerfinden.
Du prototypst nah am Code und nutzt AI-assistierte Tools aktiv, um Feedback-Loops auf Tage statt Wochen zu verkürzen.
Fundierte User-Research-Praxis: Interviews mit nicht-technischen, zeitknappen Nutzern führen und daraus Entscheidungen ableiten.
Du arbeitest gern in engen Schleifen mit Foundern und Engineering – kurze Nachrichten, schnelle Calls, Entscheidungen am selben Tag, Revert am nächsten, wenn nötig.
Du bist bereit regelmäßig mit dem Team vor Ort in Offenburg zu arbeiten oder remote mit engen Touchpoints.
Du kommunizierst fließend auf Deutsch und Englisch (beides auf professionellem Niveau).
‍
🚀 Was dich erwartet:‍
Founding-Level-Ownership: Du prägst, wie sich eine neue Produktkategorie anfühlt – nicht nur ein weiteres Feature.
Ein Problem, das sich zu lösen lohnt: Unabhängige Hoteliers bekommen zum ersten Mal die Schlagkraft eines dedizierten Revenue Managers. Echter Business-Impact, echte Menschen auf der anderen Seite.
Direkter Draht zu den Foundern: Du arbeitest täglich mit Marius (CTPO) und Sebastian – kurze Wege, echte Entscheidungen, keine Design-Hierarchie dazwischen.
Technisch wirklich ambitioniertes Produkt: Konversationelle AI in einer datendichten, hochsensiblen Domäne – hier entstehen Patterns, die es so noch nicht gibt.
Echter Zeitdruck mit echten Partnern: Committete Beta-Design-Partner warten auf Prototypen. Bis Ende 2026 nutzen erste Kunden das Live-Produkt.
Flexible Arbeitszeiten, Remote-Arbeit, persönliches Weiterbildungsbudget, Hansefit, Bikeleasing, Workation und die üblichen Benefits – aber ehrlich gesagt: wenn du wegen der Benefits kommst, bist du hier falsch.

Superhuman offers a dynamic hybrid working model for this role. This flexible approach gives team members the best of both worlds: plenty of focus time along with in-person collaboration that helps foster trust, innovation, and a strong team culture.
About Superhuman
Grammarly is now part of Superhuman, the AI productivity platform on a mission to unlock the superhuman potential in everyone. The Superhuman suite of apps and agents brings AI wherever people work, integrating with over 1 million applications and websites.

The company's products include Grammarly's writing assistance, Superhuman Docs's collaborative workspaces, Mail's inbox management, and Go, the proactive AI assistant that understands context and delivers help automatically.

Founded in 2009, Superhuman empowers over 40 million people, 50,000 organizations, and 3,000 educational institutions worldwide to eliminate busywork and focus on what matters.

s.h: Learn more at superhuman.com and about our values here .
s.t:
The Opportunity
Android is where some of the most interesting product design problems in mobile AI live right now. We’re looking for a dedicated designer who can truly own it, and leverage all that the platform has to offer. Android provides deeper OS integration and a unique floating bubble app, which provides a lot more opportunity for proactive assistance, so we want someone to drive that to its full potential.
You'll be the dedicated product designer on Android. You'll set the interaction model, the craft bar, and the design foundation the whole platform is built on for years to come.
This role is about shaping the Superhuman platform on Android. Today, that means evolving the Grammarly floating assistant that millions of people already use on their phones. The bigger work ahead is bringing Superhuman Go, our proactive AI agent, to Android with full native ambition, and pulling the rest of the Superhuman suite onto mobile alongside it.
In This Role, You Will
Set the design vision for Superhuman on Android. Define how a multi-product AI platform shows up coherently on the phone. Decide what users experience as one Superhuman, what stays distinct, and how the pieces fit together as more products move onto Android over time.
Design Go on Android. Go is our proactive AI agent, the layer that turns intent into progress across reading, writing, and communication. Shape how Go feels native to Android, where the OS lets us reach further than we can elsewhere: ambient assistance, deeper system integrations, hands-free voice flows, and proactive nudges that feel earned.
Evolve the Grammarly Android experience. Lead the next chapter of the floating writing assistant that brings real-time grammar, rewrites, translations, and tone help into any app on the phone. Sharpen the visual hierarchy, rebuild patterns for feature discoverability, and set the bar for an overlay app that people want to live with.
Help define the future input experience. Voice input is rolling out across the company, and agentic capabilities are reshaping how people write on mobile. Design how voice, agents, and the overlay come together into one coherent experience.
Establish the Android design foundation. Build the patterns, components, and onboarding framework that let Android ship faster. Decide what gets unified across platforms and what stays platform-specific.
Hold the craft line. Stay close to engineers, prototype the messy parts, and iterate until the product feels right with real text running through real models.

Senior-Level product design experience, with a portfolio that shows shipped Android work and a clear point of view on Material Design, overlays, accessibility services, and the spatial constraints of mobile.
Demonstrated craft across interaction, visual, and motion design. We care more about the polish, judgment, and ideas in your work than the company logos on your resume.
Experience designing AI-native or agent-driven products, or a strong appetite for it. Bonus if you've shipped features where model behavior, latency, or uncertainty were first-class design problems.
Fluency in prototyping as a way of thinking. Comfortable with Figma plus modern AI tools like Claude Code, and willing to push prototypes into real builds when a static mock can't answer the question.
Track record of operating independently in fast-moving environments: setting direction, managing your own priorities, and partnering productively with PMs and engineers.
Support for you, professionally and personally
Professional growth: We believe that autonomy and trust are key to empowering our team members to do their best, most innovative work in a way that aligns with their interests, talents, and well-being. We also support professional development and advancement with training, coaching, and regular feedback.
A connected team: Superhuman builds a product that helps people connect, and we apply this mindset to our own team. Our remote-first hybrid model enables a highly collaborative culture. We work to foster belonging among team members in a variety of ways.

This includes our employee resource groups, Superhuman Circles, which promote connection among those with shared identities including BIPOC and LGBTQIA+ team members, women, and parents. We also celebrate our colleagues and accomplishments with global, local, and team-specific programs.
Comprehensive benefits for candidates based in Germany: Superhuman offers all team members competitive pay along with a benefits package encompassing life care (including mental health care and risk benefits) and ample and defined time off. We also offer support to set up a home office, wellness and pet care stipends, learning and development opportunities, and more.
Relocation Support: Superhuman provides comprehensive relocation support to make your move to Berlin seamless. Our package includes visa assistance, destination services to help you and your family settle in comfortably, and a relocation bonus to cover additional expenses, such as temporary housing.
We encourage you to apply
At Superhuman, we value our differences, and we encourage all to apply. Superhuman is an equal-opportunity company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race or ethnic origin, religion or belief, gender, disability, sexual identity, or age.

About Xsolla
Xsolla is a global gaming commerce company that provides the business engine behind 2,000+ game developers and publishers worldwide. Founded in 2005, Xsolla builds the payments, storefront, and monetization infrastructure that lets game developers sell directly to players — at a global scale, across 200+ countries, 20+ languages, and 1,000+ payment methods.
Headquartered and incorporated in Los Angeles, California, Xsolla operates globally. Offices and hubs mentioned include North Carolina (US), a growing presence in Canada, Berlin, Serbia, multiple offices in China, plus Tokyo and Seoul. Teams are broadly distributed across time zones.

We are looking for a Senior Product Designer to join our Consumer Products team and shape experiences that reach players directly across web stores, loyalty programmes, and engagement surfaces that blur the line between commerce and gameplay.

In this role, you will design for real people making real decisions: whether to spend, return, share, or stay. You will work at the intersection of consumer psychology, game mechanics, and product strategy, helping build experiences that feel as rewarding as the games they support.
What You’ll Be Responsible For
Design end-to-end consumer experiences across web stores, player portals, loyalty systems, and engagement features.
Translate player psychology, behavioural data, and business goals into intuitive, high-converting design solutions.
Apply and evolve gamification mechanics such as progression systems, rewards, streaks, and social proof to drive retention and engagement.
Contribute to and evolve design principles, patterns, and system-level consistency across consumer-facing products.

8+ years of product design experience, with a focus on consumer-facing digital products.
Deep understanding of B2C UX: how people browse, decide, and transact in digital environments.
Strong knowledge of game mechanics, player psychology, and engagement design: you understand why players spend, grind, return, and churn.
Experience with gamification patterns: progression systems, battle passes, daily rewards, leaderboards, and social loops.
Strong systems thinking and visual/interaction design craft.
Comfortable working in data-driven environments: you use metrics and experimentation to validate design decisions.
Strong communication and stakeholder collaboration skills.
What You'll Need to Succeed
You are an active gamer or have a genuine passion for games and player culture.
Have shipped B2C products in gaming, entertainment, or social platforms.
Have experience designing online stores, subscription products, or loyalty/rewards programmes.
Have experience with AI-assisted design workflows or are actively curious about them.
What You'll Get
A “build the platform” moment: real influence on UX architecture as Shop Builder evolves toward self-serve.
Work at a meaningful scale, with measurable impact on conversion and partner revenue.
A strong cross-functional setup: Product, Engineering, UX Research, UX Writing, DesignOps, plus a functioning design system.
A remote-first environment with a globally distributed team and real ownership expectations.
A benefits program (healthcare, PTO, development) with specifics confirmed in process.

This is a rare chance to shape a product that sits right at the intersection of commerce psychology, platform thinking, and games. You’ll be designing for real scale (millions of transactions), real constraints (localization, regional pricing, cross‑cultural UX), and real outcomes (conversion and revenue you can actually measure).

The team is actively moving from “custom service work” toward a true self‑serve platform, which means the architecture and patterns you define will ripple across the ecosystem.

If you like being early enough to influence the direction and you’re excited about shipping faster with modern, AI‑assisted workflows alongside strong engineering partners, you’ll feel at home here.

We’re seeking a Product Designer to join our Ground Control Station (GCS) team and shape the user experience of next-generation UAS control software. This role is ideal for a systems-minded designer with a passion for solving complex UX problems in mission-critical, real-time environments.
You’ll work alongside engineers, operators, and product teams to design intuitive workflows and spatial interfaces that allow users to plan, command, and monitor autonomous assets with confidence and clarity.

Lead design efforts for key GCS capabilities, ensuring user needs are met across the full development lifecycle.
Collaborate with engineering, autonomy, product, and test teams to gather system constraints and translate them into user-centered design solutions.
Influence cross-functional planning, roadmap prioritization, and long-term product vision.
Drive the end-to-end design process—from concept, wireframes, and prototypes to detailed UI specs and implementation support.
Regularly test and iterate on designs with real users, incorporating feedback to improve usability and mission effectiveness.
Help define and maintain a coherent visual and interaction language that supports real-time control, situational awareness, and operational trust.
Advocate for operator experience and usability in high-stakes environments where clarity, speed, and precision are critical.
Contribute to the evolution of our design systems, tooling, and cross-platform interface strategy.
Travel to test flights to perform operator research and support the rollout of new GCS features.

Minimum of 5 years of design, HCI, or related experience with a Bachelor’s degree; or 4 years and a Master’s degree; or a PhD with 3 years of experience; or equivalent experience.
3+ years of experience leading end-to-end product design across complex features or products.
Proven track record designing complex, interactive systems—especially in domains involving spatial data, control interfaces, or high information density.
Demonstrated expertise in Figma as a primary design tool for creating scalable, system-driven designs.
Deep experience working within cross-functional teams, synthesizing and input from Product Management and Engineering.
Experience conducting usability testing and integrating user feedback into iterative design cycles.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to clearly articulate design rationale and tradeoffs.
Ability to work efficiently, demonstrating bias for action in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment.

Experience designing interfaces for real-time control systems (e.g., UAS, robotics, vehicles, or aviation platforms).
Familiarity with military or mission-critical systems and operator workflows.
Understanding of design constraints imposed by low-latency or high-performance software systems.
Exposure to 2D/3D mapping, telemetry visualization, or command-and-control interfaces.
Familiarity with web-based frontends (React, WebGL, etc.) or embedded UI technologies.
Familiarization with, and experience implementing, Military Standards (MIL-STDs) to product design.

At Linear, we're building the product development system for teams and agents. AI is fundamentally changing how software gets built, and we’re shaping the tools this new era requires.
Founded in 2019, Linear has become the platform of choice for more than 40,000 companies (including OpenAI, Coinbase, and Ramp) to plan, build, and ship their products. Today, our team is distributed across North America, Europe, and Australia, and we’re continuing to grow internationally. What unites us is relentless focus, fast execution, and a deep care for software craftsmanship.
Quality is our competitive advantage. Every member of our fully remote team is a maker at heart, caring deeply about the quality and feel of our work. While the industry optimizes for speed and metrics alone, we believe that craft and quality have lasting value. Quality creates gravity — it pulls people toward our team and product rather than requiring us to push. This philosophy drives everything we do, from product decisions to hiring choices.
For this role, we expect robust design skills, sharp product thinking, and the ability to engage in technical discussions. We work in small, autonomous project teams, where engineers are paired tightly with designers to explore ideas, build prototypes, deploy internal builds, and ultimately ship to customers. You will be a key element of projects from beginning to end.
Location & work mode
Linear is a remote-first company, with optional co-working offices in San Francisco, New York, and London. This role is open to candidates based in North America. You can work from anywhere within this region. We value deep focus and async collaboration, with intentional moments to connect in person through team off-sites, optional co-working, and occasional travel.

Discord has a highly engaged community of millions of daily active users who use the platform for many different reasons, but there’s one thing that nearly everyone does: play video games. Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming, and we are focused on making it easier and more fun for people to hang out before, during, and after playing games.
We're looking for a Product Designer to join Growth at Discord and help shape how people find Discord, get set up, and stay connected over time.
Growth sits at the front door of our consumer org. We're responsible for how Discord shows up in the world — how new people discover us, how they land and get started, and how existing users stay close to the conversations and communities they care about. It's a broad, fast-moving surface area, and design plays a central role in making each of those moments feel unmistakably like Discord.

s.h: This role spans the full breadth of what Growth owns
s.t:
Notifications — helping users stay connected to what they care about, even when they're away. We're making notifications more intelligent, trusted, and effective: reaching people at the right moments, coordinating delivery thoughtfully, and giving users real control over their experience.
Off-platform — how Discord shows up beyond the app itself, across embeds, links, invites, web pages, and text messages. These are often someone's first impression of Discord, and there's a lot of room to make them better.
Onboarding — rethinking how new users arrive, understand what Discord is, and find their footing in those first few minutes.
GSEO — a growing effort to build the web experiences that help new people discover Discord through search in the first place.
You won't own all of this at once, but you'll work across it — and you'll help us shape how these pieces fit together into one coherent growth experience rather than a set of disconnected products.
What You'll Be Doing
Own end-to-end initiatives across Growth — a new notification type, an onboarding flow, an off-platform surface like invites or embeds, or a web experience built to bring new users in — designing across all platforms (iOS, Android, Desktop, Web)
Design with high craft and velocity — creating production-ready specs and high-fidelity prototypes while knowing when to ship vs. polish
Influence scope and strategy in partnership with your PM, engineering lead, and cross-functional teammates, balancing growth velocity with user value
Use data and research to inform decisions, partnering with research and data science teams to validate designs and understand user behavior
Think in systems — considering how discovery, onboarding, off-platform touchpoints, and re-engagement work together to create one cohesive experience
Collaborate and communicate effectively — sharing work early and often, telling compelling stories about your design rationale, and building relationships across teams
Drive projects autonomously — managing your own time and deliverables while knowing when to escalate blockers
What you should have
3+ years of product design experience designing consumer-facing digital products — though we're open to strong candidates with 2+ years who demonstrate exceptional craft and potential.
Strong visual design foundation with demonstrated aesthetic taste. You have a high level of skill crafting beautiful interfaces and an eye for creating delight in every product experience — typography, color, hierarchy, and composition are second nature to you. You're comfortable working with design systems.
Solid interaction design skills — you create intuitive flows, understand information architecture, and can design for complex, multi-step experiences. You're comfortable designing systems, not just screens.
High proficiency with Figma and prototyping tools (Protopie, Framer, Principle, etc.) — you use prototypes to communicate your vision, test concepts, and build alignment with stakeholders.
Experience shipping products collaboratively in cross-functional teams with engineering, product management, research, and data science.
Ownership mindset with a bias toward action — you proactively drive projects and decisions forward. You help guide product vision through design explorations, documentation, and presentations.

Personal use of Discord and passion for gaming or community platforms
Experience designing growth, onboarding, acquisition, or lifecycle products
Understanding of how products reach and grow users across surfaces — notifications, messaging, web, SEO, or shareable/viral loops
Familiarity with experimentation frameworks and data-driven iteration

At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.
Lyft connects people to transportation to change the way we live and get around our communities. Lyft is North America’s leader in micromobility. We provide the software that powers BIXI, and we own and/or operate bikeshare in New York (Citi Bike), Chicago (Divvy), San Francisco (Bay Wheels), Portland (Biketown), Boston (BlueBikes), and DC (Capital Bikeshare). Our software is used in over 45 markets to power bike and scooter systems, increasing our reach beyond the markets we operate directly.
We are looking for a passionate Product Designer to join our Montreal office to work on Lyft’s micromobility Operations Technology team.
As a member of the Operations Technology team, you’ll be responsible for evolving the platform that drives the global on-the-ground operations of our business. You’ll be designing features that are used in warehouses, vans, & on-the-ground to make our transportation systems some of the most reliable in the world. You’ll confront complex technical challenges & advocate for experiences that delight our operators and promote efficiency.
Our Montreal office developed the first automated bikes-share system in North America and continues to work on the platform today that provides state-of-the-art electric bikes and scooters for tens of millions of rides per year.
As a product designer at Lyft, you will be involved at every step of product development, from brainstorming broad ideas to ensuring design quality through launch. Using your full range of interaction, visual, and product thinking skills. As a product designer on the Lyft Urban Solutions team you will own the design of features within the core rider experience for our bike and scooter riders, within the Lyft app and our market specific apps.
In a lot of ways, we function as a startup, meaning we all work closely and collaboratively across organizations to align on product vision and ship products. Our Design and Research teams live and breathe a user-centered process to create the best possible, end-to-end, experience for riders all over the world. We can be scrappy when we need to be, though we are always focused on quality and influence.

Senior Product Designer @ Secfix
Location: Remote (EMEA) · CET/CEST timezone
Hi — I'm Grigory, co-founder and CTO at Secfix.
How do you feel about owning a feature from the first customer conversation to the version that's live on production — writing the spec yourself, pairing closely with engineers through the build, and overseeing your design shipped on production exactly the way you designed it? If that sounds like the right shape of the job — designer who owns, not designer who hands off — read on.
I've spent most of my career believing the best designers aren't the ones with the prettiest Figma files. They're the ones who can frame a problem, write a spec, sit with engineers through the build, and own that what shipped is what they designed. Our founding product designer, Ghada , has been doing exactly that since we started.

The engineering team has doubled and we're shipping faster than we ever have. We're hiring the second designer because there's more good work to do than one person can hold — and we'd rather ship twice as much than slow down.
Why Secfix exists
Over 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it.
Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months.
We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to European market leadership.
This space is not threatened by AI, it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of product design work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more.
What we believe
Compliance software has historically been built like the audit it automates — heavy, defensive, ugly. We're building something else. The customer is a real person trying to ship audit-ready evidence on a Friday afternoon. The product should respect their time, automate the boring parts, and make the rest feel calm.
Quality is the product. Most of our category competes on feature lists. We compete on craft. A clear empty state, a sync that doesn't lie, a settings page that holds together at eleven permission tiers — these are the things customers feel before they can name them. Design at Secfix is not what wraps the product. It's most of what makes it work.

We expect strong design skill, strong product thinking, and the ability to hold your own in a technical discussion. You work in a small team — usually with one or two engineers — and pair closely from the first prototype through to production. You own the project from beginning to end.
Alongside the features you ship, you do three things that make everyone else faster:
Maintain the components and patterns that make design fast.
Own how the team ships. We have no PMs. You write the specs, run the ticketing workflow, keep engineers unblocked.
Build the tools and skills — Cursor rules, design QA skills, prompt templates — that let engineers do good design work without you in the room.
The leverage is doing all four well. Doing only one is the wrong shape.
How we work
No PMs. Designers and engineers run product. You talk to customers, frame the problem, write the spec, decide what ships.
Small temporary teams. You plus one or two engineers per project. Whoever is closest to the problem leads.
Design leads the logic, engineering tests feasibility. You bring the V1. Engineers push back on what's expensive or risky, start ahead with system design. They help spot edge cases. You adjust it fast. We get from v1 to v4 in matter of hours or few days.
Prototype-grade, not wireframes. Real components, real states, real copy. Sometimes an LLM-built prototype before Figma. The component library stays current because the speed of design depends on it.
Handoff is the beginning, not the end. You're in the engineering channel. You review the PR. You verify on production. Staging QA is the first gate, not the last.
In-sync culture with thoughtful coms mindset. Loom for reviews, Notion for specs, quick loops in Gather where written coms doesn’t cut it, all happening in the same time zone. Team mates are reviewing things quick. Engineers and designers spend under two hours weekly meetings.
AI is part of the craft. We use Claude to pressure-test ideas, draft specs, surface edge cases, write test cases. Not to skip thinking.
The first three months
Month 1. Ship your first design to production. Get into the codebase, the customer language, the way we write specs. Sit on customer calls.
Month 2. Own a full feature end-to-end. Customer conversations, problem framing, Figma, spec, engineer pairing, PR review, production verification.
Month 3 and beyond. Push the design system forward. Start building the tools and skills that make engineers faster at design. Improve the product design process. The bar is yours to defend.

8+ years designing B2B SaaS desktop applications as Staff/Principal Product Designer or similar. Dense interfaces — tables, filters, permissions, settings pages.
You've been the only designer, or one of two or three, in companies under 50 people at least once before. You know how to set the bar without a design org behind you.
Your portfolio is "I," not "we." You can name the engineer you paired with on each feature, the design decision you defended through the build, and what happened when the feature reached users.
You communicate clearly and concise in English: in Slack, in docs and on a call.
You're fast in Figma with or without AI. You’re already in a serious relationship with LLMs.
You treat engineering feasibility as input, not constraint. When an engineer says "three weeks, here's why," you find the version that's 80% as good and ships next week.
You're comfortable doing product work without the PM title.
You hear feedback and come back the next day with something better. You don't spend the hour in between defending the version that's already outdated.

Leading product design on projects - defining vision, direction and outcomes

Translate complex technologies, audience insights and stakeholder ambitions into elegant, intuitive digital experiences - combining strong design craft with a clear sense of purpose

Create momentum and alignment from ambiguity - guiding multidisciplinary teams and clients with confidence and clarity

Mentor and support designers across levels, offering constructive feedback, guidance and opportunities for growth.

Contribute to shaping the product design discipline at BB: introducing new tools and workflows, sharing perspectives, and maintaining a high standard of craft.

Collaborate with peers across disciplines to strengthen how we work together and deliver exceptional outcomes.

Represent BB’s product design practice in client conversations, articulating ideas clearly and persuasively.

Work closely with ambitious clients pushing the limits of their fields - from early-stage startups to industry leaders

6+ years of product design experience, with deep expertise across design and technology

We are hiring a Product Designer with 2 to 5 years of experience to carry well-scoped, ongoing work on a mature product under senior review, so the senior designers can focus on the new bet.

This is deliberately the first seat below Senior on the team: a place to do real craft on a real product, with strong people to learn from, and a clear path toward Senior. What you'll do:
Own well-scoped, ongoing design work on a mature product area (likely Deploy): iterations, improvements, edge cases, polish, and consistency work, with review and direction from a Senior or Staff Designer.
Turn defined problems into clear, production-ready interface designs. Strong fundamentals in interaction design, information architecture, and visual design. Share examples of this work through a portfolio or concrete work samples during the process.

Partner with engineering and PM through implementation. Pair on edge cases. Communicate decisions with reasoning, not preference.
Contribute design assets to launches and releases (in-product onboarding, release-notes visuals, announcement surfaces) with guidance.
Build technical fluency. Be curious about DevOps, IaC, and the dense, technical workflows our users live in, even when it is new to you.

2 to 5 years of product design experience, ideally on B2B, technical, or developer-facing products.
Solid fundamentals in interaction design, information architecture, and visual design.
Fluency in Figma and modern design system practice.
A portfolio or work samples with concrete examples we can review, showing shipped product work, design process, interaction decisions, and visual craft. Applications without examples or a portfolio will not be considered.
Reliable on ongoing, iterative work. You finish things, you sweat the details, and you keep quality consistent across a lot of small surfaces.

s.h: About the role: What's in the box
s.t:
HelloFresh Group is building the next generation of consumer experiences across its portfolio — from discovery and personalisation to shopping and subscription management. The Consumer UX team is at the heart of this work, designing end-to-end experiences that are simple, delightful, and grounded in real customer needs.
We're hiring Senior UX Designers across two squads: one embedded in Good Chop , our premium American meat and seafood subscription brand, and one in our central Consumer UX team working across the broader HelloFresh Group portfolio. Both roles share the same craft bar, strategic expectations, and ways of working — the difference is context and squad focus.
These are full-ownership roles in a startup-paced environment. You'll partner with Product and Engineering on a cross-functional squad — the PM owns the roadmap, you own the UX direction. UX here is a strategic input, not a downstream service.

Consumer Experience Design: Lead design from concept to shipped product, maintaining accountability for the full consumer experience across touchpoints. You hold a high bar for quality at every stage — from early framing through final execution.
Strategy and Roadmap Influence: Frame problems before they become briefs. Bring evidence-backed consumer insight into squad planning — challenge priorities, surface opportunities, and influence what gets built. You're a strategic partner in roadmap conversations, contributing to direction from the start.
Craft and Execution: Hold a high personal bar across UI, interaction design, motion, micro-interaction, and UX writing — and raise the standard within your squad. Use animation and motion as intentional tools, not decoration.
AI-Native Workflow: Use AI across the full workflow — synthesis, discovery, rapid prototyping, design-to-code. A working method that lets you move faster and think sharper.

Experience: 6+ years in product design, with a proven track record delivering high-quality consumer products end-to-end.
Consumer Instinct: You've worked on consumer-facing products and understand how real people make decisions — to try something, to stay, to leave. You think about the full customer lifecycle, not just the next feature. Subscription context is a plus.
Strategic Range: You define the problem before designing the solution. You've pushed back on a brief, reframed a PM's question, or changed a roadmap priority through evidence. You bring design into the strategy conversation because you built the case, not because you were invited.
Craft Mastery: Exceptional visual and interaction design skills with a high personal bar. Deep focus on hierarchy, motion, micro-interaction, and animation. Figma mastery is non-negotiable. You understand front-end constraints well enough to have credible conversations with engineers.
High Agency: Proactivity to push for the right solution rather than the convenient one, with conviction in your design decisions and the ability to bring cross-functional partners along.
Research Fluency: You can frame a research question, run a lightweight study, and translate findings into design direction without needing a researcher to drive the process. You know when to go deeper and how to collaborate with experts.
AI-Native in Practice: Active use of AI tools in live project work — synthesis, discovery, prototyping, design-to-code. Fluency with tools like Figma AI and Claude is expected. This is how you work, not something you're working towards.
Communication: You present clearly, facilitate alignment across functions, and can run a workshop as confidently as you can ship a screen. You make the case for your decisions with evidence, not opinion.

Join Proton and build a better internet where privacy is the default
Proton was founded in 2014 by scientists from CERN on a simple truth: privacy is a fundamental human right . Since then, we've built the world's largest encrypted email service (Proton Mail) and expanded into Proton VPN, Proton Drive, Proton Pass, and Proton Calendar — tools used by millions globally to protect their freedom, fight censorship, and keep their data safe. In some situations, Proton has literally helped save lives.
We are profitable, independent (no VC control), and selectively hire from the top ~1% of applicants. Our 700+ team members across 50+ countries come from leading organizations and elite academic backgrounds. We move fast, keep hierarchy light, and prioritize impact over optics. If you want to do meaningful work with exceptionally high-caliber people, this is it. Check our open-source projects here .
The Design Team
Proton's Design team shapes the visual and interaction layer across Mail, Drive, VPN, Pass, and Calendar — products used by millions of people, many of whom rely on them in high-stakes moments.

About Bonusly
Bonusly is the recognition and rewards platform people actually use. We believe culture is built by everyone, not assigned by HR. Our AI companion, Bizy, helps people recognize each other better and helps leaders understand what's really happening across their organization.To learn more about working at Bonusly , check out our Un-Handbook:
Why this role exists
Our Insights business unit is one of our biggest bets: turning recognition data into strategic intelligence that helps leaders understand team health, engagement, and culture in real time. We're building AI-powered products (generative UIs, conversational analysis, culture visualizations) that surface patterns no survey could capture. The design conventions don't exist yet. We have to invent them.
The gap we're filling is creative energy. We're looking for someone who stretches us visually with fresh, imaginative ideas and a consumer sensibility that makes B2B software feel alive. You'll work alongside a product leader, an engineering leader, and another designer who leads the Insights BU, while collaborating with designers and engineers across the company.
